steps.label: Compute before save
steps.description: Live progress rises during compute. No new checkpoint has completed yet.

steps.label: Complete first save
steps.description: Progress stays flat during the save. Only the completed write publishes the first durable restore point.

steps.label: Compute the next interval
steps.description: The live run advances, while the previous durable point remains unchanged.

steps.label: Complete second save
steps.description: After the second write verifies and its manifest is published, durable progress advances to the new save boundary. No save occurs during subsequent compute.

steps.label: Accumulate unsaved progress
steps.description: The red rising segment is live progress after the last completed save. Failure can discard this whole interval.

steps.label: Failure rolls back progress
steps.description: At failure, live progress drops vertically to the last durable level. The discarded interval is rework; it is distinct from restart latency.

steps.label: Recover without progress
steps.description: Selecting the published checkpoint manifest, loading its snapshot, scheduling, and warmup consume recovery time while progress stays flat. The completed save already identifies the restore point.

steps.label: Resume productive compute
steps.description: After recovery, computation advances again from the durable level. The failure costs both the lost interval and recovery; save overhead is paid separately at each checkpoint.
